tldr: The FCC conditionally approved SpaceX's Starmind, the first US licence for an orbital compute constellation, with up to 1 million satellites carrying ~175 kW of compute each. Separately, OpenAI posted a 111-page preprint claiming the matrix-multiplication exponent is exactly 9/4, though it has not been peer-reviewed.

Huang affair: Reuters says the DOJ never formally investigated Jensen Huang before his reinstatement, and that firms linked to Alice Huang pledged $270M of AI servers held in China as loan collateral. USTR proposed Section 301 'overcapacity' tariffs on 14 economies, with Taiwan, Korea and Japan facing up to 15% (chips appear exempt).

AI chip stocks fell sharply: KOSPI dropped 6.16% as SK hynix lost 11%, Taiex fell 4.8% and Nvidia ended down 3.9% at $149.30. In Hong Kong, Zhipu fell 15% and MiniMax 13.8% as Apple pulled MiniMax's Talkie companion app worldwide.

items.title: FCC approves SpaceX's Starmind: up to 1 million orbital data-centre satellites for AI compute
items.summary: On Nov 25 the FCC conditionally authorised SpaceX's Starmind constellation of up to one million orbital compute satellites. This is the first US licence for a constellation built for in-orbit computing. The satellites are designed to carry an average 175 kW compute payload (up to 250 kW), sit at 500-1,002 km altitude, and link by laser. SpaceX must start deploying by November 2033, reach 10% (100,000) by November 2035 and 50% by November 2038. Amazon had asked the FCC to reject the application as 'lofty ambition rather than a real plan', and astronomers raised congestion and debris concerns.
items.why_it_matters: The approval gives the regulatory basis for moving AI compute off the power-constrained grid and into orbit, though no satellites have launched.
key_numbers: 175 kW avg compute payload (up to 250 kW)

items.title: OpenAI preprint claims the matrix multiplication exponent is exactly 9/4, adding a matching lower bound
items.summary: OpenAI posted a 111-page preprint, 'The matrix multiplication exponent is nine fourths', claiming that omega = 9/4 over every field. It pairs the 9/4 upper bound from OpenAI's October 2 preprint (which covered only the complex numbers) with a new lower bound for formal arithmetic circuits: for n >= 2, at least ceil(n^(9/4)/2) nonscalar multiplication or division gates are needed. The preprint and a Lean formalization sit in the openai/math GitHub repo. The Lean proof covers only division-free circuits, a narrower scope than the paper's main theorem.
items.why_it_matters: If it holds, AI-assisted work would settle a complexity question open since about 1969. The proof is unreviewed and only partly machine-checked, and it does not make practical GPU matrix multiplication any faster.

items.title: Reuters: DOJ never formally investigated Jensen Huang before Trump pushed for his reinstatement
items.summary: Three people told Reuters that the Justice Department ran no formal investigation and no counterintelligence probe of Jensen Huang before Trump pressed Nvidia's board to reinstate him. Attorney General Todd Blanche based his conclusion that there was no evidence Huang broke the law on DOJ probes of two Nvidia customers, Super Micro and Megaspeed. Vice President Vance separately said DOJ and national-security officials had assured him Huang was not under investigation, which conflicts with Trump's earlier statement that there was one. Treasury Secretary Bessent's 10-day deadline for Nvidia's board to answer export-control questions also ended on Nov 25 with no public response.
items.why_it_matters: This weakens the official account behind Huang's ouster and return just before his Dec 1 House interview and Dec 3 Senate hearing.

items.title: USTR proposes Section 301 'overcapacity' tariffs of up to 35% on 14 economies incl. Taiwan, Korea, Japan
items.summary: USTR issued determinations in 14 of its 16 Section 301 investigations into structural excess manufacturing capacity and proposed tariffs on China, the EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, India, Vietnam and others. The EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan and Switzerland face up to 15% net of MFN and existing duties, with higher alternative ceilings (Korea and Taiwan up to 25%). Five Southeast Asian economies plus Bangladesh face up to 18% and Vietnam up to 35%. Baker McKenzie says goods already under Section 232 tariffs, which include semiconductors, are exempt for 13 of the 14 economies. Comments are due Jan 5 and hearings begin Jan 25, 2027. Market reports linked the proposal to Wednesday's chip-stock sell-off.
items.why_it_matters: Chips appear to be carved out, but the findings name semiconductors as a sector of concern for Japan, Korea and Taiwan, which adds trade risk for the AI hardware supply chain.
key_numbers: Up to 15% for Japan/Korea/Taiwan/EU (alt. up to 25% Korea/Taiwan)

items.title: METR analyses OpenAI's published loss data: pretraining loss falling about 7x faster since early 2026
items.summary: METR published 'Interpreting a recent acceleration in pretraining loss', analysing OpenAI's newly released loss figures for 13 models since GPT-3.5, all measured on one held-out set of OpenAI's own source code. Its two-segment fit puts the log-perplexity decline at about 0.022 per year before a February 2026 breakpoint and about 0.156 per year after it, roughly 7x faster. At that pace, the GPT-3.5-to-GPT-4.1 gain would repeat in about 6.5 months. METR says its staff have no consensus on what this means, and asks labs to share loss on other datasets plus compute and labour data.
items.why_it_matters: It is the first outside read of proprietary frontier pretraining data, and it suggests pretraining progress may be speeding up rather than plateauing, though the data rests on a single code corpus.

items.title: PrismML releases Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, a 5.9 GB open-weight ternary model tuned for coding agents and tool use
items.summary: PrismML released Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B under Apache 2.0. It upgrades Ternary Bonsai 2 27B and is built on Qwen3.8 27B, with ternary weights averaging about 1.76 bits that fit in roughly 5.9 GB. PrismML reports an agentic-coding average of 54.2, up from 37.9 for Bonsai 2, and a tool-calling average of 82.2, up from 60.2. It runs on Nvidia and Intel GPUs through llama.cpp and on Apple devices through MLX, with about 291 tokens/s on one H100 using multi-token prediction.
items.why_it_matters: It puts a 27B-class agentic coding model on a laptop at roughly a ninth of its FP16 size, which makes private, local coding agents more practical.

items.title: Google DeepMind releases 'Humanity's First Exam', a 544-prompt test of whether models answer easy questions reliably
items.summary: DeepMind published Humanity's First Exam (HFE) on Kaggle. It has 544 easy text and image prompts across 20 foundational capabilities, grouped into 136 families of four near-identical variants; a family counts only if a model gets all four right across repeated runs. The top five models score 96-98% on single attempts but average 85.6% at family level, and visual perception causes about three-quarters of errors. 112 prompts are public under CC BY 4.0, and a Kaggle contest for everyday questions models still fail runs to Dec 15.
items.why_it_matters: It moves evaluation from peak capability to reliability on trivial tasks, a gap that matters for deployed agents.

items.summary: On Zhihu's Q3 2026 earnings call, CEO Zhou Yuan addressed the company's RMB1.5bn commitment to Monolith's Tianjin Lisi Xingshen fund, which has taken a low-single-digit stake in DeepSeek. He called it a long-term strategic decision that would not come at the expense of the core business, financial soundness or shareholders, and said share buybacks will continue. Q3 revenue was RMB659M, roughly flat year on year. The net loss was RMB48.56M (adjusted RMB30.77M), and average monthly subscribing members rose 7% quarter on quarter to 14.1 million. Cash, deposits and short-term investments totalled RMB4.24bn at the end of September.
items.why_it_matters: The call sizes the Zhihu deal that briefly made it a listed proxy for DeepSeek. A RMB1.5bn commitment is more than a third of Zhihu's cash pile.

items.title: Tencent releases GGUF quantised weights for its 224B Hy4 flash, saying it runs on a 64GB Mac mini
items.original_title: 让大模型跑在个人设备上，腾讯混元开源 Hy4 flash GGUF 量化权重及配套推理代码
items.summary: Tencent Hunyuan released GGUF quantised weights and inference code for Hy4 flash (224B parameters) through its AngelSlim compression toolkit, on Hugging Face and ModelScope under AngelSlim/Hy4-flash-GGUF. Variants include Q4_K_M, Q3_K, IQ2-AH and two 4-bit builds for DGX Spark. The smallest, about 125.73 GiB, is roughly 30% of the original's ~410 GiB. Tencent says an optimised Strata offload framework lets it run on a 64GB Mac mini, that Q3_K reaches about 47 tokens/s at 32K context on an M5 Max with 128GB, and that Q3_K stays within 0.4 points of the full model on four evals.
items.why_it_matters: It brings a frontier-class Chinese open model to high-end personal hardware. This follows Hy4 flash's strong OpenRouter debut.

items.summary: On Nov 25 Moonshot AI launched Kimi Voyager, an international hiring programme to recruit 20 overseas business partners and build a global ecosystem around its open-source Kimi models. The roles include applied AI architects for enterprise API onboarding, developer relations, global PR, brand marketing, design, 'Country Launcher' roles to open new national markets, and an exploratory 'Wild Card' role. Both experienced-hire and internship positions are open.

learn.title: Fit a hinge regression to find where a training-loss trend breaks
learn.why_today: METR fitted a two-segment trend to OpenAI's log-perplexity data and reports the decline speeding up from about 0.022 to about 0.156 per year after a February 2026 breakpoint.
learn.explanation: A hinge (segmented) regression models y = a + b1 t + b2 max(0, t - tau), so the slope is b1 before tau and b1 + b2 after it, with the curve continuous at tau. For a fixed tau this is ordinary least squares, so you can grid-search tau and keep the fit with the lowest squared error. The catch is that tau is chosen to fit the data: with few points (METR had 13 models), the breakpoint and the post-break slope have wide, non-Gaussian uncertainty, and a smooth acceleration or one outlier near the end can look like a sharp break. Report a bootstrap or profile-likelihood interval for tau and the slope ratio, and compare the fit against a single line and a smooth curve with an information criterion before calling it a regime change. The snippet uses synthetic data, not OpenAI's numbers.
learn.math: y_i = a + b_1 t_i + b_2 \max(0, t_i-\tau) + \varepsilon_i,\quad \hat\tau = \arg\min_\tau \mathrm{SSE}(\tau)
learn.python:
# Fit a two-segment (hinge) linear trend to log-loss vs time and find the breakpoint.
# Synthetic, illustrative data only (not OpenAI's or METR's numbers).
import random
random.seed(0)
t = [2022 + 0.25 * i for i in range(20)]              # years
true_bp, a, s1, s2 = 2026.1, 1.20, -0.02, -0.15
y = [a + s1 * (x - 2022) + (s2 - s1) * max(0.0, x - true_bp) + random.gauss(0, 0.01) for x in t]

def ols(X, y):  # tiny normal-equations solver for 3 params
    n = len(X[0]); A = [[sum(r[i] * r[j] for r in X) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]
    b = [sum(r[i] * yy for r, yy in zip(X, y)) for i in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):  # Gaussian elimination
        for k in range(i + 1, n):
            f = A[k][i] / A[i][i]
            A[k] = [ak - f * ai for ak, ai in zip(A[k], A[i])]; b[k] -= f * b[i]
    c = [0.0] * n
    for i in reversed(range(n)):
        c[i] = (b[i] - sum(A[i][j] * c[j] for j in range(i + 1, n))) / A[i][i]
    return c

best = None
for bp in [2023 + 0.05 * k for k in range(70)]:
    X = [[1.0, x - 2022, max(0.0, x - bp)] for x in t]
    c = ols(X, y)
    sse = sum((yy - sum(ci * xi for ci, xi in zip(c, r))) ** 2 for r, yy in zip(X, y))
    if best is None or sse < best[0]:
        best = (sse, bp, c)
sse, bp, c = best
print(f"breakpoint ~ {bp:.2f}; slope before {c[1]:.3f}/yr, after {c[1]+c[2]:.3f}/yr, ratio {(c[1]+c[2])/c[1]:.1f}x")

learn.title: Work out the real bits per weight of a ternary model, scales included
learn.why_today: PrismML says Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B averages about 1.76 bits per weight and fits in roughly 5.9 GB.
learn.explanation: A ternary weight takes one of {-1, 0, +1}, so its information content is log2 3 ≈ 1.585 bits. Real formats need byte-friendly packing: 5 trits fit in one byte because 3^5 = 243 ≤ 256, which gives 1.6 bits. Each group of weights also needs a higher-precision scale, adding scale_bits/group bits per weight. Layers kept at higher precision, such as embeddings, norms and the output head, push the average up further. That is why reported figures land a little above 1.585. Memory is roughly params × bits / 8 bytes plus the KV cache and activations, so a weight-only number understates what inference needs. The group size and scale format in the snippet are assumptions, not PrismML's spec.
learn.python:
# Bits per weight of a ternary model, and what fits in memory.
# Illustrative arithmetic; group size and scale format are assumptions, not PrismML's spec.
import math
params = 27e9
ideal = math.log2(3)                       # entropy bound for {-1, 0, +1}
packed = 8 / 5                             # 5 trits per byte: 3^5 = 243 <= 256
group, scale_bits = 128, 16                # one fp16 scale per 128 weights (assumed)
eff = packed + scale_bits / group
for name, b in [("fp16", 16), ("int4", 4 + 16 / 128), ("ternary, ideal", ideal),
                ("ternary, 5-per-byte + scales", eff)]:
    print(f"{name:30s} {b:6.3f} bits/w  -> {params * b / 8 / 1e9:6.2f} GB")
print("reported: ~1.76 bits/w, ~5.9 GB ->", round(params * 1.76 / 8 / 1e9, 2), "GB")

learn.title: Predict 'all k variants correct' accuracy from per-prompt accuracy
learn.why_today: Humanity's First Exam counts a family of four near-identical prompts only if all four are right; top models score 96-98% on single prompts but average 85.6% at family level.
learn.explanation: If errors were independent with per-prompt accuracy p, a family of k variants would pass with probability p^k, so 0.97^4 ≈ 0.885. Errors are usually correlated within a family: if a model can't do the task, it misses all variants. For a fixed mean p, this concentration raises family accuracy above p^k (by Jensen's inequality on q ↦ q^k), up to p when errors cluster completely. So a family score at or below p^k means the model is failing variants it 'should' get right, which is exactly the inconsistency the metric targets. Repeated runs add sampling noise as another source of variation. The snippet uses illustrative numbers, not HFE data.
learn.python:
# Family-level ('all k variants right') accuracy vs per-prompt accuracy p.
# Illustrative numbers only. Families are a mix of easy and hard ones with the same mean accuracy p.
p, k = 0.97, 4
print(f"independent errors: p^k = {p**k:.3f}")
for f_hard in (0.03, 0.06, 0.15, 0.5):           # share of families that are 'hard'
    q_hard = 0.0 if f_hard <= 1 - p else 1 - (1 - p) / f_hard   # hard-family accuracy
    q_hard = max(q_hard, 0.0)
    q_easy = (p - f_hard * q_hard) / (1 - f_hard) if f_hard < 1 else p
    if q_easy > 1: continue
    fam = f_hard * q_hard**k + (1 - f_hard) * q_easy**k
    print(f"hard share {f_hard:.2f}: q_hard={q_hard:.2f} q_easy={q_easy:.3f} -> family pass {fam:.3f}")
# Monte Carlo check of the independent case
import random; random.seed(1)
n = 100_000
mc = sum(all(random.random() < p for _ in range(k)) for _ in range(n)) / n
print(f"Monte Carlo (independent): {mc:.3f}")
